claims.text: The initial high-entropy alloy is a single-phase solid solution.
Formation of nanoscale precipitates is responsible for toughness loss or brittle fracture during mechanical loading.
Nanoscale precipitates act as stress concentrators.
Stress concentration around nanoscale precipitates produces localized plastic deformation.
Stress concentration and localized plastic deformation promote crack initiation.
Crack initiation associated with precipitates leads to loss of toughness or brittle fracture.
The proposed behavior applies at temperatures below 500 degrees Celsius.
The proposed behavior applies at stresses above 500 MPa.
The proposed behavior applies at strain rates above 10^-3 per second.
An alloy condition containing nanoscale precipitates can be mechanistically compared with a precipitate-free condition using tensile, fracture-toughness, and TEM measurements.
Similar toughness in the precipitate-free condition would falsify the proposed precipitate-mediated mechanism.
Improved toughness in the precipitate-free condition would falsify the proposed precipitate-mediated mechanism.
The specific alloy composition and processing history are not sufficiently characterized.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts that precipitates degrade toughness, so improved toughness in the precipitate-free control would support—not falsify—the proposed precipitate-mediated embrittlement mechanism. Only no meaningful toughness difference, or worse toughness after precipitate removal under an otherwise valid control, would challenge it.
